title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Territorial Jurisdiction over Patent Infringement Disputes
keywords_en: patent right; People's Court concerning patent infringement dispute
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issues Concerning Territorial Jurisdiction over Patent Infringement Disputes

Fa (Jing) Fa [1987] No. 17

To all local high people's courts and intermediate people's courts throughout the country, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army and the military courts of all major units, all railway transport intermediate courts, and all maritime courts:

Our court's Fa (Jing) Fa [1985] No. 3, the "Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Conduct of Patent Trial Work," has provided rules on jurisdiction over patent dispute cases. We now provide supplementary provisions on territorial jurisdiction over patent infringement dispute cases as follows:

1. Where, without the permission of the patentee, a patented product for invention or utility model is manufactured, used, or sold, or a patented product for design is manufactured or sold, for production and business purposes, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the product is manufactured; if the place of manufacture is unknown, the case shall be accepted by the people's court of the place where the product is used or sold.

2. Where, without the permission of the patentee, a patented method is used for production and business purposes, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the user of the patented method is located.

3. Where a person, without authorization from the patentee, licenses or commissions another to exploit the patent, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the licensor or the commissioning party is located; if the licensee or the commissioned party has exploited the patent, thereby constituting joint infringement with the other party, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the licensee or the commissioned party is located.

4. Where a co-owner of a patent right, without the consent of the other co-owners, licenses another to exploit the patent, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the licensor is located; if the licensee has exploited the patent, thereby constituting joint infringement with the licensor, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the licensee is located.

5. Where a co-owner of a patent right, without the consent of the other co-owners, transfers a share of the patent right exceeding his or her due share, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the transferor is located; if the transferee knowingly accepts the transfer in excess of authority, thereby constituting joint infringement with the transferor, the case may be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the transferee is located.

6. Where a person counterfeits the patent of another, which does not yet constitute a crime, but causes damage to the patentee or an interested party, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the counterfeiting act occurred or where the result of the damage occurred; if this is difficult, the case may be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the defendant is located.

When determining territorial jurisdiction in accordance with the above items, the provisions on the designation of jurisdiction over cases as set out in our court's "Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Conduct of Patent Trial Work" shall still be applied.

June 29, 1987
